included: governance schemas, scripts, policies and exact commit manifest
scope.git_worktree_scope_validation: NOT_EXECUTED because repository-wide Git enumeration could disclose prohibited sibling paths; implementation was statically reviewed.

findings.evidence: The Phase 1 lock is checked only against task-intent scope. Blueprint product/database flags and write paths are not bound to phase-status.authorized_paths or the intent/classification scope. Change-scope subsequently trusts those Blueprint paths.
findings.reproduction: A structurally complete L3 fixture can retain intent product_changes_allowed=false while assigning frontend-engineer and setting Blueprint writes to frontend/**. Role policy permits that path, so validateTask and validateChangedPaths have no Phase 1 rejection.
findings.impact: A crafted Task can bypass the Phase 1 governance-only product lock and authorize product changes.

findings.evidence: NOT_APPLICABLE requires only a truthy waiver object. No alternative control is required, approved_by and approver_role are unbound strings, approval timing is not compared with scope approval, and L3 non-waivability is inferred only from requirement_id text.
findings.reproduction: Mark an opaque required integrity ID NOT_APPLICABLE, provide a waiver attributed to an agent with an approval time after final approval and no alternative control, and use another PASS artifact for final prerequisites. The non-waivable regex does not match the opaque ID and no gate reason is added.
findings.impact: Required or non-waivable L3 evidence can be waived without prior scoped human authority or compensating control.

findings.evidence: scope_validation and preapproval_gate accept any PASS check or artifact ID. They are not bound to a validate-change-scope result, staged file set, manifest hash or distinct preapproval execution. Change-scope itself exits successfully as NOT_A_COMMIT_CANDIDATE when no product file is staged.
findings.reproduction: Observed serial case 01 returned GO while both prerequisites referenced generic EV-FIXTURE; no Git scope validation or exact staged 87-file proof existed.
findings.impact: Final commit approval can pass without an exact staged manifest candidate or deterministic preapproval gate.

findings.evidence: Chronology is calculated only from stages with status=approved. execution_approval=not-required is accepted for non-sensitive work but filtered out of the ordered timestamps and is not checked against implementation start.
findings.reproduction: Move the complete GO fixture's not-required execution decision to a timestamp after review_completion or final_commit_approval. Existing checks still accept the Task.
findings.impact: The fixed scope, execution decision, review completion and final approval ordering can be bypassed.

findings.evidence: Distinct test checks sharing a requirement_id are rejected, but duplicate artifact_id values are not. validArtifactEvidence is a Set, so multiple artifacts with the same required ID collapse to one accepted verdict.
findings.reproduction: Add two valid, different artifact records sharing ART-FIXTURE. Both scan successfully, the Set retains one ID, and required verdict count remains one.
findings.impact: Evidence identity uniqueness and conflict traceability can be bypassed.

findings.evidence: The parent harness accepts at least 25 cases rather than exactly 50, and artifact_hashes_structured passes vacuously when no case supplies a hash.
findings.reproduction: A child report containing 25 passing cases and no artifact hashes satisfies the current reportsValid and deterministicArtifacts expressions.
findings.impact: The harness can claim complete structured concurrency proof from a partial or hash-free child report, although this A3 execution did produce two real 50-case reports.

findings.evidence: The 87-file candidate still records active_remediation_task=GOV-PHASE1-REMEDIATION-2 and session_a2_started=false despite completed A2, Remediation 3 and the A3 scaffold.
findings.reproduction: Compare phase-status.json with the filed GOV-PHASE1-L3-REVIEW-A2, GOV-PHASE1-REMEDIATION-3 and GOV-PHASE1-L3-REVIEW-A3 task directories.
findings.impact: The committed lifecycle status would be stale, although both governance and Migration 320 gates correctly remain NO-GO.

conditions: Bind all Blueprint scope and write paths to the active Phase 1 lock and add a product-write rejection fixture.
Require waiver alternative controls, prior scoped human approval, authority binding and semantic non-waivable categories.
Bind scope and preapproval prerequisites to structured, hash-bound executions proving staged_manifest_mode=EXACT.
Include not-required execution decisions in chronological ordering and require them before implementation start.
Reject duplicate artifact IDs and add artifact/check conflict fixtures.
Require exactly 50 concurrency cases and at least one expected structured artifact hash per child.
Refresh phase-status and rerun an independent baseline-bound review.

decisions_required.decision: Keep the Phase 1 Governance Commit Gate at NO-GO and authorize remediation plus a fresh independent review.
Keep the separate Migration 320 Gate at NO-GO; this review does not approve migration, product, database, commit, merge or release activity.

residual_risks: Passing fixtures do not cover the reproduced fail-closed bypasses.
Reviewer context isolation and human identity remain procedural rather than cryptographically proven.
The deterministic scanner cannot establish global secret absence.
Actual repository-wide staged scope was not enumerated because sibling path disclosure was prohibited.
No product test, service, database, seed, migration or Git mutation was performed.
